watch.what: Bids close for the European Union's AI gigafactories: up to seven, in Europe's push for computing power of its own.
The AI Act's rules for high-risk uses (hiring, credit, education, policing, border control) begin to apply.
watch.evidence: Systems listed in Annex III now have until 2 December 2027

watch.what: The same rules reach AI built into products that EU safety law already covers.
watch.evidence: those covered by the product-safety laws in Annex I until 2 August 2028

watch.what: Whether the Clay Institute accepts the machine-found Navier–Stokes proof, and whom it credits.
watch.evidence: its rules ask for a refereed publication and two years of acceptance before a committee even meets

watch.what: Whether an open-source agent, run offline, takes ARC-AGI-3's grand prize.
watch.evidence: Its grand prize, $700,000 for the first agent to score 100%, is a different contest

watch.what: Whether the European Commission's questions about the summer's incidents end in the AI Act's first fine on the maker of a general-purpose model, and whether the Act reaches a model still under test.
watch.evidence: the Commission can fine the maker of a general-purpose model up to 3% of its worldwide turnover

watch.what: How the suits over ChatGPT are decided, Florida's and eight other states' among them: the first tests of who answers for what a chatbot says.
watch.evidence: Florida sued alone in June; in October eight states sued on one day

watch.what: Whether the laboratories' call to pace the frontier together gets the government support it asked for.
watch.evidence: each laboratory may slow itself, and the country will not
